corrected_recommendation: Keep the central pick: mlx-community/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base via mlx-audio >= 0.5.1 with ICL cloning (ref_audio + ref_text), stream=True, streaming_interval=0.32. Do not use VoxCPM2 for this slot. Amend four things. (1) Stay on -8bit; do NOT "pick bf16 for quality" as the memory section directs — bf16 is unmeasured on this box and doubles bytes-read per decode step in a bandwidth-bound loop that I measured at RTF 0.76-0.92 with a single competing GPU process. VoxEMW's bf16 warning ("generation can't keep up with playback") describes exactly the margin that is already thin here; treat it as an open A/B, not a resolved artifact. (2) Delete the "6-bit repo is gone / mac_setup.sh will fail" risk and the matching evidence item. mlx-community/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base-6bit returns HTTP 200 with 449 downloads, and a -5bit exists too; VoxEMW's scripts/mac_setup.sh line 54 and the config's auto-mapping to 6bit both work as written. No mlx_quantization override is required. (3) Replace the "0.7-1.4 s mouth-close to first audio" budget. It omits endpointing/turn-detection entirely and assumes STT 0.2-0.4 s, while the same machine's own ASR runs (adv_bench.log, bench_contended.log, Qwen3-ASR-1.7B) show p50 0.60-1.18 s and p90 up to 2.06 s for the 6-9 s debate turns this app actually sees. A defensible budget is turn-detect (0.2-0.8 s) + STT (0.6-1.2 s p50, ~2.1 s p90) + LLM first sentence (unmeasured) + TTS TTFA (0.13-0.42 s). TTS is not the bottleneck, but the sub-2 s end-to-end target is not demonstrated and likely fails at p90 unless STT is chunked to overlap with user speech. (4) State the contended numbers in the verdict, not only in open_questions: RTF degrades from 0.33-0.52 idle to 0.76-0.92 with one contender, so the "2.4x ahead of playback, will not underrun" headline is really ~1.1x margin in the real pipeline. Budget a jitter buffer and re-measure with the actual LLM resident. Barge-in, which the finding never addresses, does work: aborting the generator after the first chunk returns in 0.142-0.181 s and the next call's TTFA is unaffected.

problems.problem: The claim that mlx-community/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base-6bit was removed from Hugging Face (404) is false. It is cited as a 'strong' evidence item, promoted to the #1 risk, and used to assert that VoxEMW's scripts/mac_setup.sh 'is broken as written' and that the user 'must set qwen3_tts_mlx_quantization explicitly or startup will fail'. All of that downstream advice is wrong. The finding is also internally inconsistent: it separately quotes mlx-audio's own qwen3_tts README benchmark as '(6-bit, batch 1): TPS 20.8, 1.67x realtime, avg TTFB 84.8 ms, 3.88 GB' — a 6-bit measurement it elsewhere says cannot exist.
problems.evidence: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://huggingface.co/api/models/mlx-community/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base-6bit -> HTTP 200. HF search API for author=mlx-community returns FIVE variants, not the three claimed: -4bit 784, -5bit 76, -6bit 449, -8bit 4084, -bf16 13575. The three download counts the finding quotes (13575/4084/784) are exactly right, so the search was run and the 6bit and 5bit rows were dropped. ./ref-VoxEMW/scripts/mac_setup.sh:54 does pin -6bit, and configs/assistant.yaml relies on auto-mapping to 6bit ('Apple Silicon 自动映射到 mlx-community 6bit 版'), so both work today. Scratchpad q3readme.md:117-121 is the 6-bit benchmark table the finding cites.

problems.problem: The latency_estimate asserts a full-pipeline budget of 'roughly 0.7-1.4 s mouth-close to first audio, comfortably inside your 2.0 s target with headroom'. This is the one number that answers the hard requirement, and it is not supported. It omits endpointing/turn-detection latency entirely (mouth-close to end-of-turn-detected is not free), and its 'STT ~0.2-0.4 s' term is contradicted by measurements sitting in the same scratchpad on the same machine.
problems.evidence: .cache/research (Qwen3-ASR-1.7B MLX, same M5 Max): clip u1 (6.35 s) clean p50 733.6 ms / p90 1146.1 ms; clip u4 (8.94 s) clean p50 888.5 ms / p90 1303.7 ms, and at 0 dB SNR p90 2158.8 ms / max 4586.2 ms. bench_contended.log: u4 p50 1180.1 ms / p90 2059.5 ms. Only the 1.4 s clip lands in the assumed 0.2-0.4 s band (p50 96-225 ms). A debate reply follows a 6-9 s user turn, so the correct STT term is 0.6-1.2 s p50, ~2.1 s p90 — 2-5x the assumed value. The scratchpad also contains smart-turn-v3/ and silero-vad-v5/, i.e. a turn detector whose latency is nowhere in the budget.

problems.problem: The verdict headline ('RTF 0.41-0.53 ... generation stays roughly 2.4x ahead of playback and will not underrun') is an idle-GPU number presented as the operating characteristic. GPU contention is demoted to an open_question, but it is the binding constraint and it roughly halves the margin. This matters because the same finding then recommends bf16, which moves in the same direction.
problems.evidence: I measured it directly (verify_contend_tts.py / verify_contend.log, same box, same model/quant/ref). IDLE: ttfa 0.133/0.169/0.203/0.156 s, rtf 0.327/0.524/0.336/0.351. With ONE sustained fp16 matmul contender (28x 4096x4096 chain, ~LLM-decode load) started 6 s earlier: ttfa 0.418/0.342/0.362/0.309 s, rtf 0.920/0.886/0.919/0.757. TTFA degrades ~2.3x and RTF ~2.2x, leaving ~1.1x margin over playback rather than 2.4x. A real build adds Qwen3-ASR plus (in VoxEMW's design, configs/assistant.yaml) a MiniCPM-V-4.6 VLM sidecar on the same Metal device.

problems.problem: The memory_gb section directs 'pick bf16 for quality unless an A/B shows no audible difference', and the why-section dismisses VoxEMW's bf16 warning as 'a 16 GB base-M5 memory-bandwidth artifact'. bf16 was never measured on this machine — the finding says so itself in open_questions — so the directive rests on inference. The inference is also pointed the wrong way given the contention data: bf16 roughly doubles weight bytes read per autoregressive step in a bandwidth-bound decode that is already at RTF ~0.9 under load.
problems.evidence: open_questions: 'bf16 vs 8-bit on this machine ... but I did not measure bf16 here.' The dismissed warning is configs/assistant.yaml line 55 in the ref repo: '# mlx_quantization: bf16  # 别升：实测 TTFA 翻倍且生成跟不上播放（内存带宽 2.6x）' — i.e. the observed failure was specifically 'generation can't keep up with playback', the exact failure mode my contended RTF 0.76-0.92 measurement shows is close at hand. No bf16 weights are present in the scratchpad models/ directory, so nothing was run.

problems.problem: Barge-in is a stated hard requirement of the build and appears nowhere in the finding — not in the verdict, evidence, risks, or open_questions. Mid-utterance abort semantics for a Python generator driving Metal kernels is a real question (does close() leave MLX stream state dirty? does the next call's TTFA regress?) and it was not asked.
problems.evidence: Full text search of the finding: no occurrence of 'barge', 'interrupt', 'abort', or 'cancel'. The reference repo does implement barge-in and its TTS handler polls a cancel token inside the generation loop (voxemw/pipeline/tts_voxcpm2.py:125 'if self.cancel_scope is not None and self.cancel_scope.discarding'), with voxemw/gateway/audio_pacer.py:8 documenting flush-on-barge-in — so the requirement is live in the codebase being ported. I tested it and the recommendation passes: break-after-first-chunk then generator.close() returns at 0.180/0.142/0.142 s, and the immediately following full generation is normal (ttfa 0.136 s, rtf 0.394). No state leak. The conclusion is unaffected; the omission is a gap in the review, not in the model.

problems.problem: The reported idle RTF band 0.41-0.53 is narrower than the model's actual run-to-run spread, because it comes from a single trial per sentence. Repeats show meaningfully more variance, which matters when the contended figure sits near 1.0.
problems.evidence: verify_q3.log, 3 repeats per sentence: 72-char sentence rtf 0.316 / 0.631 / 0.413; 88-char 0.392 / 0.392 / 0.441; 173-char 0.409 / 0.387 / 0.414. Measured idle band is 0.316-0.631, not 0.41-0.53; the single-trial 0.631 outlier is a 1.5x spread on the same input. TTFA reproduces well (0.125-0.228 vs claimed 0.157-0.256) and peak memory reproduces (3.97 GB vs claimed 3.94 GB).

problems.problem: VoxCPM issue #293 is misdescribed. The finding characterizes it as documenting 'streaming degrading from 0.3 s/chunk to 1-2 s/chunk after 400+ chunks from an O(max_length) attention mask', cited as a strong-strength reason to avoid the PyTorch/MPS path.
problems.evidence: GitHub API for OpenBMB/VoxCPM issue 293 returns title 'MiniCPM4 `forward_step` Attention Performance Fix', state open, created 2026-05-04. That is a perf-fix proposal for an attention step, not the streaming-degradation bug report described. Every other cited issue checked out exactly — #910 'Qwen3-TTS ICL voice cloning progressively accelerates speech pace on long texts (suspected: forced repetition_penalty floor of 1.5)' closed 2026-08-26; #921 open 2026-08-28 with the exact title quoted; PR #914 merged; #557 open; VoxCPM #337 open 2026-06-08; #232 closed; PR #263 'fix(mps): force float32 on Apple Silicon' merged; QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS #341 open with the exact reference-tail-echo title; resemble-ai #424 open. So this is an isolated slip, not a pattern.

problems.problem: The '97 ms first-packet latency' evidence item omits that the figure is a CUDA measurement, which is the specific extrapolation trap this review was asked to check. The paper states it was produced on an internal vLLM engine with torch.compile and CUDA Graph acceleration. Presenting it in a list of Apple Silicon evidence invites the reader to treat it as achievable here.
problems.evidence: arxiv.org/html/2601.15621v1: 'based on our internal vLLM engine (vLLM V0 backend) on a single typical computational resource with optimizations applied via torch.compile and CUDA Graph acceleration to the decoding stage of the tokenizer.' The 97 ms / 101 ms figures and the streaming design claim are otherwise quoted accurately. This does not affect the recommendation, which correctly rests on the author's own MLX measurements (0.13-0.42 s TTFA), roughly 2-4x the CUDA number.

problems.problem: Breeze TTS 2 is identified by the finding's own evidence as one of only three mlx-audio models with BOTH zero-shot cloning and chunked streaming — the exact intersection that decides this slot — and then never appears in alternatives, is never benchmarked, and is never ruled out with a reason.
problems.evidence: The finding's evidence item quotes the official table as 'Qwen3-TTS Yes/Yes; Breeze TTS 2 (1B, EN+ZH) Yes/Yes; CSM/MisoTTS (1B/8B, EN) Yes/Yes'. I confirmed that table (scratchpad ttsindex.md: '| [**Breeze TTS 2**](breeze-tts.md) | 1B | EN, ZH | Yes | Yes | Voice design, cloning, direction, and inline vocal events |'). CSM gets an alternatives entry; Breeze TTS 2 gets none. Separately, the finding quotes the on-device-ai table but silently drops its fastest row, Supertonic 3 at 1.1 s / 0.55 GB — defensible on the merits (its open weights ship fixed preset voices; zero-shot cloning is a separate hosted Voice Builder service, so it cannot fill this slot) but it should have been named in the ruled-out list rather than omitted.

problems.problem: The 'output verified real audio' check validates only that the model is not producing silence; it says nothing about clone fidelity, because the reference clip is itself a macOS `say` synthetic voice rather than a human recording. The finding does flag subjective fidelity as its top open question, but the verification language ('not the historical silent-clone failure mode', peak 0.723 / RMS 0.154) reads stronger than what was tested. Related: the Chatterbox Turbo alternative was never measured on this box.
problems.evidence: scratchpad ref_raw.aiff is 'IFF data, AIFF-C compressed audio' written at 15:19, one minute before ref_en.wav — the signature of `say -o`. ref_en.wav is 7.798 s at 24 kHz, matching the '7.8 s' claim. For Chatterbox Turbo, I ran the author's own bench_cb.py against models/chatterbox-turbo-fp16 and it fails at load: 'RuntimeError: [load_safetensors] Tensor s3gen.decoder.estimator.mid_blocks.6.transformer_blocks.0.attn1.to_out.0.weight invalid data offsets (182728976, 183253264) exceeding the size of the file. Perhaps an incomplete download' — so that alternative rests entirely on third-party numbers, as the finding implies but does not state.

surviving_claims: Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base-8bit streams cloned English on this M5 Max at sub-0.3 s TTFA with RTF well under 1.0 on an idle GPU. Independently reproduced with my own script: TTFA 0.125-0.228 s, RTF 0.316-0.631, 12-29 chunks per utterance, peak 3.97 GB (claimed 0.157-0.256 s / 0.41-0.53 / 3.94 GB). Load 1.66 s, warmup under 1 s once weights are cached.

mlx-audio's VoxCPM2 port has no chunked streaming, and the mechanism is exactly as described. Verified in the installed mlx-audio 0.5.3 source: mlx_audio/tts/models/voxcpm2/voxcpm2.py has generate() with no `stream` parameter, `audio = self.audio_vae.decode(all_feats_flat)` at line 677 after the full AR loop, and a single `yield GenerationResult(...)` at line 700; audio_vae exposes only encode()/decode()/preprocess()/sanitize() with no streaming_decode or decode_chunk. `streaming_prefix_len` (line 415) only sizes continuation context. mlx-audio's own docs table lists 'VoxCPM2 | 2B | 30 languages | Yes | --'.

VoxCPM2 via mlx-audio emits one chunk per utterance on this machine, so TTFA equals whole-utterance generation time: 4.647 / 7.333 / 11.209 s for 72/88/173-char inputs, chunks=1 in every row, peak 6.84 GB (stage2.log). Warm re-runs at inference_timesteps=10 give RTF 0.889-1.048 with marginal RTF 0.829 (bench3.log). This is 20-45x worse TTFA than the recommended path and over any sub-3 s ceiling on its own.

This is a genuine capability gap on Apple Silicon rather than a tuning problem: the upstream PyTorch voxcpm package streams via `with self.audio_vae.streaming_decode() as vae_dec: vae_dec.decode_chunk(...)`, and that state machine simply has no MLX counterpart.

Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base is English-SOTA on Seed-TTS-eval test-en. Verified against arXiv 2601.15621 Table 5, which reproduces every quoted number exactly: Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base 0.77|1.24, 12Hz-0.6B-Base 0.92|1.32, CosyVoice 3 0.71|1.45, MiniMax-Speech 0.83|1.65, F5-TTS 1.56|1.83, Spark TTS 1.20|1.98, Seed-TTS 1.12|2.25. The paper's own text confirms 'state-of-the-art performance on the test-en set with a WER of 1.24' and the highest speaker similarity across all 10 languages vs MiniMax and ElevenLabs. VoxCPM2 is absent from that table, and the finding is transparent that its 1.84 comes from VoxCPM2's own report (arXiv 2606.06928, real).

The 0.6B-vs-1.7B tension the finding surfaces is real and correctly quoted. arXiv 2601.15621 Table 6 English row: content consistency 12Hz-0.6B 0.836 vs 12Hz-1.7B 0.934; speaker similarity 0.829 vs 0.775 — i.e. the 0.6B wins on the multilingual test while the 1.7B wins on Seed-TTS test-en. Leaving this as an A/B rather than asserting bigger-is-better is the right call.

No CUDA-only dependency breaks the recommended path. The recommended stack is pure MLX/Metal with no flash-attn, Triton, bitsandbytes, xformers, DeepSpeed, TensorRT, or vLLM anywhere in it; the only CUDA-gated capability in the comparison is VoxCPM2's streaming AudioVAE, which the finding correctly identifies as the reason to reject that model on this hardware.

The PyTorch/MPS route for VoxCPM2 is worse than the MLX route, as claimed. OpenBMB/VoxCPM PR #263 'fix(mps): force float32 on Apple Silicon to avoid bf16 quality loss' is merged, issue #232 'NotImplementedError: Output channels > 65536 not supported at the MPS device' is real, and issue #337 'voxCPM2.0版本暂不支持mac M芯片mps加速' is still open (created 2026-06-08).

The tokenizer trap is real and correctly documented. stage2.log captures the exact failure: 'Warning: Could not load tokenizer ... You need to have sentencepiece or tiktoken installed' at load, followed by a clean load and then 'ValueError: Tokenizer not loaded. Call post_load_hook first.' at qwen3_tts.py:633 on the first cloning call. With tiktoken installed my re-run proceeds normally. The install_commands correctly list tiktoken/sentencepiece/protobuf as required and not auto-pulled.

The ICL cloning caveats and version pin are accurate. mlx-audio #910 (pace acceleration from the repetition_penalty floor, closed), PR #914 (merged, 'window ICL repetition penalty to stop pace acceleration'), #921 (open, ref_text not covering full ref_audio causes no-EOS degeneration), #557 (open, CustomVoice ignores clone refs), and QwenLM/Qwen3-TTS #341 (open, 'Voice-clone (ICL) generation echoes the tail of the reference audio before the requested text') all exist with the titles described. Pinning mlx-audio >= 0.5.1 and requiring an exact whole-clip transcript are correct.

The independent third-party direction check is quoted accurately. on-device-ai.com/posts/2026-05-26-tts-comparison/ gives Chatterbox 8-bit 1.9 s / 2.04 GB, Qwen3-TTS 0.6B 8-bit 3.4 s / 2.11 GB, Qwen3-TTS 1.7B 8-bit 4.4 s / 3.15 GB, VoxCPM2 4-bit 10.2 s / 2.49 GB, VoxCPM2 8-bit 10.5 s / 3.35 GB, with the verdicts 'Its speed is in the upper quartile' (Qwen3) and 'The quality is good, but unfortunately its speed is not as strong' (VoxCPM2).

The characterization of the reference repo's Mac choices is correct. ref-VoxEMW/configs/assistant.yaml sets tts.backend: qwen3 with model_name Qwen/Qwen3-TTS-12Hz-1.7B-Base on Mac, while configs/assistant-4090.yaml sets tts.backend: voxcpm2 — exactly the split the finding describes, including the commented-out bf16 line with its stated reason.
Kokoro is correctly ruled out for this slot: mlx-audio's table marks it '--' for both Voice Cloning and Streaming (82M, 54 voice presets), so it can only serve as a non-cloned fallback voice.

Barge-in works on the recommended path, though the finding never checked it: breaking out of the streaming generator after the first chunk and calling close() returns in 0.142-0.181 s, and the next full generation is unaffected (TTFA 0.136 s, RTF 0.394), so mid-utterance interruption is clean at ~0.32 s chunk granularity.
